newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB makes new headway, sets new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB makes new headway, sets new all-time high.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract made new headway in uncharted territory after setting a new all-time high for any benchmark futures contract by Monday's Tokyo close.
The December ended at 124.74, after setting a new record high of 124.96. It closed at 124.49 on Friday.

"Chasing the bull-run of the futures market, investors bought cash JGBs (with life remaining to maturity) of seven years and longer, flattening the longer-end of the yield curve," a city bank trader said.
Dealers are reluctant to hold fresh short positions ahead of an expected shift of the benchmark to the March contract in mid-November, adding to the bullish tone of the market.
"After a chaotic short-squeeze in the September (contract), nobody is comfortable carrying fresh short positions for long ahead of the benchmark shift," a brokerage trader said.
The squeeze drove up the lending rate for the cheapest 161st 10-year JGB deliverable against the September to a stunning 32 percent at one point, traders said.
Demand to cover short positions built in December prior to the recent rally remained in the market, they said.

The cheapest deliverable issues against the December were the 164th, 166th and 167th JGBs. So far, there had been no sign of a short squeeze in the market as liquidity in those issues was ample, traders said.
However, some foreign speculators had already begun to buy the cheapest JGBs deliverable against the March, they said.

In the cash market, the 182nd JGB had failed to break below its yield of 2.600 percent by late-afternoon Tokyo as large institutional investors, such as pension funds, set their profit-taking target at that level, traders said. The yield of the 182nd 10-year JGB was 2.610 percent at 0622 GMT.
Kazuto Uchida, chief strategist for Tokyo-Mitsubishi Securities Co Ltd's trading division, said: "The most significant factor behind the market's current firmness is the supply and demand balance."

The JGB market stands to be the main beneficiary of the government scheme to clear up the bad loan mess at Japan's mortgage firms, traders said. Some of the funds set up under the scheme have already poured massive amounts of cash into JGBs, including through some purchases of JGBs offered this month. Traders said there was also potential demand from institutional investors slow to catch the recent bond rally.
The Ministry of Finance is expected to offer 500 billion yen worth of six-year JGBs on Tuesday.
It is expected to carry a 1.9 percent coupon and healthy investor demand is anticipated, traders said.
